description: Combined Geotechnical and Geophysical Investigation of Texas Rivers Post Hurricane Harvey is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Nina Stark, University of Florida (ufl.edu). Hurricane Harvey caused severe wind damages and flooding in Fall 2017. In fact, the associated flooding can be classified as a 5,000 year event. Associated to the flooding, significant sediment relocation processes occurred. Sediment erosion around submerged structures and foundations, commonly referred to as scour, represents a significant risk to the stability of infrastructures. Coverage: multiple locations in Texas. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: geotechnical, geophysical, river flooding. Published 2020-04-02. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
